issues.description: The UML diagram in the problem statement defines the class as 'Course' while the rest of the description, the template, and the solution all refer to and implement a class named 'Lecture'. This naming mismatch in the problem statement's UML can confuse students about which class they are expected to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the UML diagram in problem_statement.md to use the class name 'Lecture' (instead of 'Course') so the diagram and the textual instructions match the template and solution. Alternatively, change the textual references to match the UML if the intent was to name the class 'Course'.

issues.description: The UML diagram in problem_statement.md defines the class as 'Course' while the problem text, the template Java file and the solution Java file refer to the same conceptual entity as 'Lecture'. This mismatch between 'Course' and 'Lecture' can confuse students trying to map the UML to the provided code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the class name consistent across artifacts.
